title: Posterior contraction in Gaussian sequence inversion

items.title: Posterior contraction rate in a Gaussian sequence inverse experiment
items.statement:
Let $\mathbb N=\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$. For each positive noise level $\epsilon$, let $\Pi_{0,\epsilon}$ be a proper Borel prior on $\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$ in the Gaussian sequence inverse experiment, and let $\mathbb P_{\Pi_{0,\epsilon}}$ be the resulting prior-predictive joint law of parameter and data. A posterior kernel is a data-measurable assignment $y\mapsto\Pi_\epsilon(\cdot\mid y)$ of Borel probability measures on $\ell^2$ satisfying
$$\mathbb P_{\Pi_{0,\epsilon}}(\theta\in A,\,Y\in B)=\int_B\Pi_\epsilon(A\mid y)\,\mathbb P_{\Pi_{0,\epsilon}}^Y(dy)$$
for every Borel $A\subseteq\ell^2$ and every product-Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}$, where $\mathbb P_{\Pi_{0,\epsilon}}^Y$ is the prior-predictive data marginal. Fix a truth $\theta^\dagger\in\ell^2$ and write $\mathbb P_{\theta^\dagger}^\epsilon$ for its data law. Since a conditional-law version is specified only up to a prior-predictive null set, any contraction claim under $\mathbb P_{\theta^\dagger}^\epsilon$ refers to the stated version. A positive function $r_\epsilon\to0$ is a posterior contraction rate in the $\ell^2$ norm at $\theta^\dagger$ if, for every positive function $M_\epsilon\to\infty$,
$$\mathbb E_{\theta^\dagger}^\epsilon\!\left[\Pi_\epsilon\!\left(\{\theta\in\ell^2:\|\theta-\theta^\dagger\|_2>M_\epsilon r_\epsilon\}\mid Y\right)\right]\longrightarrow0\quad\text{as }\epsilon\downarrow0.$$

references.title: B. T. Knapik, A. W. van der Vaart, and J. H. van Zanten, Bayesian inverse problems with Gaussian priors, The Annals of Statistics 39 (2011), §4, Theorem 4.1
references.locator: Theorem 4.1 states expected posterior tail convergence outside M_n times a rate for every M_n tending to infinity.

references.title: Iain M. Johnstone, Gaussian estimation: Sequence and wavelet models, 2013 draft
references.locator: §2.3, printed pp. 25–29, for product priors/posteriors and posterior risk terminology.

items.axiom_use: No additional axiom is required to define this rate; a posterior kernel and the sequence experiment are inputs.

items.title: Exact posterior second moment and contraction bound for a Gaussian sequence inverse problem
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $0<\epsilon$, let $(s_j)_{j\ge1}$ be the positive singular values in the Gaussian sequence inverse model, and let a fixed truth $\theta^\dagger=(\theta^\dagger_j)_{j\ge1}$ belong to $\ell^2(\mathbb N_{>0},\mathbb R)$. Let $\tau_j>0$ satisfy $\sum_{j\ge1}\tau_j^2<\infty$, and let the prior be a Borel probability on $\ell^2$ whose coordinates are independent $N(0,\tau_j^2)$ variables, independent of the observation noise. Under the prior-predictive law the observations are $Y_j=s_j\theta_j+\epsilon\xi_j$; under the fixed truth they are $Y_j=s_j\theta^\dagger_j+\epsilon\xi_j$, where the $\xi_j$ are independent $N(0,1)$ variables. Define $v_j=(\tau_j^{-2}+s_j^2/\epsilon^2)^{-1}$ and $\lambda_j=\tau_j^2s_j^2/(\epsilon^2+\tau_j^2s_j^2)$. For fixed-truth-almost every data sequence, a posterior version on $\ell^2$ is the restriction of $\bigotimes_{j\ge1}N(\lambda_jY_j/s_j,v_j)$. Its expected posterior squared distance from the truth is
$$S_\epsilon(\theta^\dagger):=\mathbb E_{\theta^\dagger}\!\left[\int_{\ell^2}\|\theta-\theta^\dagger\|_2^2\,\Pi_\epsilon(d\theta\mid Y)\right]=\sum_{j\ge1}\left[(1-\lambda_j)^2(\theta^\dagger_j)^2+\frac{v_j^2s_j^2}{\epsilon^2}+v_j\right].$$
The identity holds in $[0,+\infty]$; under the stated trace condition its right side is finite. For every $R>0$, the expected posterior mass outside the radius-$R$ ball is at most $S_\epsilon(\theta^\dagger)/R^2$. In particular, if $S_\epsilon(\theta^\dagger)\le C r_\epsilon^2$ for a constant $C$ and a positive $r_\epsilon\to0$, then $r_\epsilon$ is a posterior contraction rate in the sense of the preceding definition.

references.title: B. T. Knapik, A. W. van der Vaart, and J. H. van Zanten, Bayesian inverse problems with Gaussian priors, The Annals of Statistics 39 (2011), 2626–2657
references.locator: §3, Proposition 3.1; §4, Theorem 4.1; §7.1 complete proof, with the diagonal coordinate expressions and sum bounds in Lemmas 8.1–8.2. The present coordinatewise trace identity is proved locally.

references.title: Iain M. Johnstone, Gaussian estimation: Sequence and wavelet models, 2013 draft
references.locator: §§1.2 and 2.3, equations (1.4), (2.14)–(2.20), and the product-prior discussion (2.16), printed pp. 6 and 25–29.

references.title: Litao Ding and Peter Mathé, Minimax rates for statistical inverse problems under general source conditions
references.locator: §1, equations (1)–(3), PDF pp. 1–2, for the sequence inverse experiment and its compact-SVD convention; no Bayesian contraction claim is taken from this minimax paper.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the compact-SVD sequence model. AC is used to construct the countable Gaussian product law. The posterior-moment, nonnegative-series, and Markov calculations use no stronger choice principle.

title: Posterior contraction in Gaussian sequence inversion — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Polynomial singular-value decay and a power Gaussian prior
items.statement: Assume AC and Countable Choice. Fix $\alpha,\beta,p,L>0$. For each $0<\epsilon\le1$, use the centered Gaussian Borel prior on $\ell^2$ with independent coordinates $\theta_j\sim N(0,j^{-1-2\alpha})$, independent of the observation noise. Under the fixed-truth law, observe $Y_j=j^{-p}\theta^\dagger_j+\epsilon\xi_j$ with independent $N(0,1)$ noise and a fixed truth $\theta^\dagger$ in the power ellipsoid $\{\theta\in\ell^2:\sum_{j\ge1}j^{2\beta}(\theta_j)^2\le L^2\}$. Then the posterior contracts in the $\ell^2$ norm at rate $r_\epsilon=\epsilon^{2\min(\alpha,\beta)/(1+2\alpha+2p)}$, meaning that for every $M_\epsilon\to\infty$ the expected posterior mass outside radius $M_\epsilon r_\epsilon$ tends to zero as $\epsilon\downarrow0$.

references.title: B. T. Knapik, A. W. van der Vaart, and J. H. van Zanten, Bayesian inverse problems with Gaussian priors, The Annals of Statistics 39 (2011), 2626–2657
references.locator: Assumption 3.1, Theorem 4.1(i), and §7.1 proof, printed pp. 8–9 and 20–21, for polynomial singular-value decay, power prior variances, and the regularity dependence; the exact bound here is proved locally.

references.title: Iain M. Johnstone, Gaussian estimation: Sequence and wavelet models, 2013 draft
references.locator: §2.3, equations (2.19)–(2.20) and product-prior discussion (2.16), printed pp. 26–29, for coordinatewise Gaussian posterior mean and variance.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the sequence model and used by the compactness and nuclear trace-class criteria. AC constructs the Hilbert Gaussian prior and is assumed by the conjugate posterior theorem. The dyadic cutoff and moment bounds use no additional choice principle.

items.title: Exponential singular-value decay and an exponentially weighted truth class
items.statement: Assume AC and Countable Choice. Fix $\alpha,\beta,p,L>0$. For each $0<\epsilon<1/e^{\alpha+p}$, use the centered Gaussian Borel prior on $\ell^2$ with independent coordinates $\theta_j\sim N(0,e^{-2\alpha j})$, independent of the observation noise. Under the fixed-truth law, observe $Y_j=e^{-pj}\theta^\dagger_j+\epsilon\xi_j$ with independent $N(0,1)$ noise and a fixed truth $\theta^\dagger$ in the exponential ellipsoid $\{\theta\in\ell^2:\sum_{j\ge1}e^{2\beta j}(\theta_j)^2\le L^2\}$. Then the posterior contracts in the $\ell^2$ norm at rate $r_\epsilon=\epsilon^{\min(\alpha,\beta)/(\alpha+p)}$, meaning that for every $M_\epsilon\to\infty$ the expected posterior mass outside radius $M_\epsilon r_\epsilon$ tends to zero as $\epsilon\downarrow0$.

references.title: Litao Ding and Peter Mathé, Minimax rates for statistical inverse problems under general source conditions
references.locator: §3 and Table 1, PDF pp. 5–6, for exponential singular-value and source-axis regimes in the minimax setting; the posterior rate here is proved locally.

items.title: A point-mass Gaussian prior excluding the truth prevents contraction
items.statement: Assume AC and Countable Choice. In every positive-noise Gaussian sequence inverse experiment, every proper centered Gaussian prior on $\ell^2$ yields posterior contraction at some rate $r_\epsilon\to0$ about every truth $\theta^\dagger\in\ell^2$, including truths for which the prior gives zero mass to every ball of radius less than $1$ centered at $\theta^\dagger$.

references.title: B. T. Knapik, A. W. van der Vaart, and J. H. van Zanten, Bayesian inverse problems with Gaussian priors, The Annals of Statistics 39 (2011), 2626–2657
references.locator: §3, Proposition 3.1, and §4, Theorem 4.1, for the positive trace-class Gaussian prior and truth-smoothness assumptions; the point-mass support boundary is proved locally.

items.axiom_use: AC and Countable Choice are stated for consistency with the sequence model and the theorem whose scope is contrasted. The point-mass posterior identity and one-coordinate likelihood-ratio calculation use no additional choice principle.
